newsitem.title: VIETNAM: IFC backs three projects, opens office in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: IFC backs three projects, opens office in Vietnam.

text.p: The International Finance Corp (IFC), an affiliate of the World Bank, said on Tuesday it would provide funds for three new projects in Vietnam and open an office in Hanoi.

IFC executive vice-president Jannik Lindbaek told reporters at a signing ceremony the corporation would make its debut in Vietnam's financial sector, helping the country establish its first leasing company.
"IFC's investment of $15.75 million will play a pioneering role in the establishment of a leasing industry," Lindbaek said.
"It will also support small and medium-sized enterprises, the backbone of Vietnam's non-state sector and the main engine for economic growth."

The IFC said its financing package for the Vietnam International Leasing Company Limited (VILC) would consist of a loan of up to $15 million, with up to $5 million for the IFC's own account, and up to $10 million for the account of project participants.
IFC will also invest $750,000 for a 15 percent equity stake
VILC's local sponsor is the Industrial and Commercial Bank of Vietnam, the largest industrial financing institution in the country.
The technical partner and main equity holder is Korea Industrial Leasing Corporation. Nippon Credit Bank of Japan and Banque Francaise du Commerce Exterieur will also be equity holders.

Lindbaek said the IFC would also launch the Mekong Project Development Facility (MPDF), an IFC-managed and donor agency-funded project which will assist in the promotion of small and medium-sized businesses in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia.
The IFC will contribute $4 million to the facility's five-year $25-million budget. Donors including Australia, Norway, Sweden and Switzerland, will provide the balance.
The IFC will also extend $5 million in seed capital for project finance to small and medium-sized enterprises through the Mekong Financing Line to help mobilise additional capital.

The third project is an agreement to provide $14.5 million in loans to San Miguel Haiphong Glass Company (SMHG), a private sector-led joint venture, for a $32-million glass container manufacturing plant in Haiphong, northern Vietnam.
The total loan package consists of a loan for IFC's account of $10 million and a syndicated loan of $4.5 million for the account of a project participant.

Project sponsors include San Miguel Holdings and San Miguel Glass Vietnam. Both are wholly owned by the Philippines-based San Miguel Corporation, which owns 65 percent of SMHG. The Vietnamese sponsor is Haiphong Glass Factory, a Vietnamese government entity.
